feedback.delta: Add a risk-sensitive perceptual evidence-floor oracle across H-WP-07-MICRO-VISUAL-LEARNER, H-WP-10-EFFECT-AUTHORITY and H-WP-14-FUZZ-ADVERSARIAL. Test false KNOWN_HIGH outputs with valid capabilities; high-consequence commit must not rely solely on familiarity support.

Preserve direct capability separation, but bind high-consequence visually conditioned effect proposals to fresh action-specific observation or an equivalent deterministic precondition receipt. Familiarity may guide routing but is not sufficient epistemic support by itself.

Attempt implementation first with existing typed/effect basis: PerceptualBasis/risk/evidence-floor metadata carried to EffectIntent/commit. No surface-language semantic change is justified by this synthetic result.

Safe-Effect geometry should distinguish authority closure from epistemic-action closure: a capability-safe system can still execute a wrong authorized action when a weak perceptual basis determines intent.

Action consequence/risk should prevent a calibrated familiar-local path from becoming an unexamined causal basis for high-consequence action. Where the evidence floor is unmet, buy deeper perception and/or workspace resources.
Represent familiarity/prototype support as derived activation evidence distinct from fresh sensor evidence and preserve links showing which basis actually supported an effect proposal/commit.

Persist perceptual-basis identity, capture epoch/freshness, classifier/calibration version, support tier, risk class, required evidence floor and commit linkage so replay can distinguish familiarity support from current observation.
Existing conflict/set-valued preservation remains compatible; no new higher-order coupling claim follows from this safety counterexample.

The synthetic safety counterexample is not evidence for or against causal emergence. It only constrains experimental/action semantics so future intervention results are not confounded by weak perceptual bases.
